description: We are Team Dynamo, a passionate and driven engineering tech team participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We combine rigorous technical execution with creative problem-solving to tackle complex aerospace and terrestrial challenges.
summary:
Signal Trust – Mission Control is a telemetry verification platform designed to prevent ground teams from acting on delayed, noisy, or misleading spacecraft data. In spaceflight operations, crew-health and life-support decisions often fail due to time confusion, missing environmental context, and misplaced trust in degraded sensors.   
To solve this, the platform routes every incoming sensor reading through a three-pillar streaming pipeline before reaching operator dashboards:   
Time Anchor: Separates true event time data as LIVE, DELAYED, or REPLAY.   
RadContext: Attaches orbital position, radiation flux, and space-weather flags (such as South Atlantic Anomaly passes) to distinguish radiation-induced hardware glitches from biological illness.   
Signal Trust: Evaluates freshness, cross-sensor consistency, signal noise, and duplicate rejection to assign a trust score.
Trusted readings are evaluated against anomaly rules for alerts, while untrusted readings trigger escalation for manual or backup checks—ensuring every operator decision is backed by an auditable, additive metadata trail.
details:
1. Time Anchor: Separates true event time from arrival time, syncs clocks, and reorders late packets (LIVE, DELAYED, or REPLAY).
    2. RadContext: Attaches orbital position and space-weather/radiation flags (such as South Atlantic Anomaly passes) to separate radiation glitches from medical or hardware issues.
    3. Signal Trust: Evaluates freshness, cross-sensor consistency, noise, and duplicates to assign a 0–1 trust score (TRUSTED, STALE, UNVERIFIED, or CORRUPTED). Trusted data triggers anomaly alerts, while untrusted data escalates for manual or backup verification.
  • Benefits & Impact: Eliminates false alarms from delayed playback, prevents stale telemetry from masking real emergencies, and replaces manual cross-checking with an auditable evidence trail to protect astronaut safety during communication disruptions.
  • Tech Stack: Built with Python (FastAPI, NumPy, SciPy, pandas, scikit-learn) and Node.js on the backend; React/Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and D3.js/Recharts on the frontend; Apache Kafka/MQTT, TimescaleDB/InfluxDB, PostgreSQL, Redis, and WebSockets for real-time streaming; and Docker/PyTest/Figma for deployment, testing, and design.
  • Creativity & Team Considerations: Uses non-destructive additive tagging, interdependent pillar scoring (where lag or radiation lowers trust), and "fail-visible" escalation. The team modeled the platform around real historical spaceflight incidents (such as Apollo 15 and ISS EVA 23), statistical false-alarm tuning, and role-based workflows for flight surgeons, controllers, and mission leads.
